1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with reasonable letter and line spacing, though it is not identifiable as a specifically dyslexia-optimised font.

2.why: Text is sentence case with no italics or all-caps, but by step 8 eight identical error banners stack into a visually dense repetitive column.

3.why: The single-column layout fits a mobile viewport, but the accumulating error banners push the form and primary button progressively further down the screen.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Sign in to start your security setup' and 'Check your email and password, then try again' are short and plain.

5.why: An example is shown under the email field ('Example: marcus@example.com') and the demo credentials are displayed as a concrete input example.

6.why: No long blocks of text appear anywhere; the longest element is a two-line demo info box.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control is visible for the demo password, and no long codes or secrets ever appear because the flow never advances past sign-in.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is shown on any of the eight screens.

9.why: The hint 'Use your saved password' and the standard email/password fields suggest password-manager and autofill support, though autocomplete attributes cannot be confirmed visually.

10.why: 'Step 1 of 4 · Sign in' is shown at the top and the large blue 'Sign in' button is visually prominent, though later steps require scrolling to reach it.

11.why: The only action requested on every screen is the single 'Sign in' button.

12.why: Each attempt produces feedback, but the message only implies failure, never states what happened, and identical duplicates stack up to eight times.

13.why: The user retries sign-in eight times with no lockout or penalty visible, though no reveal/hide or re-request controls are present.

14.why: The error 'Check your email and password, then try again' is non-blaming and suggests a fix but never specifies which field or what actually went wrong.

15.why: No timers, countdowns, or auto-dismissing elements are visible on any screen, though the code-entry step is never reached so its timing cannot be confirmed.
